questions.e: The Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS), 2023 replaces the Indian Penal Code of 1860, expanding from 511 to 358 sections while adding new offences like terrorism and mob lynching.

questions.q: The Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita was first introduced in Parliament as a Bill in —
questions.e: The BNSS Bill was introduced in the Lok Sabha in August 2023 along with the BNS and BSA Bills; all three were passed in December 2023 and came into force on 1 July 2024.

questions.subject: Polity
questions.q: The Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam (BSA) replaces —
questions.e: The Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam (BSA), 2023 replaces the Indian Evidence Act, 1872, giving legal sanctity to electronic and digital records as primary evidence.

questions.subject: Polity
questions.q: What is the maximum punishment for mob lynching under the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita?
questions.e: Section 103(2) of the BNS prescribes the death penalty or life imprisonment for mob lynching committed by a group of five or more on grounds of race, caste, community, sex or place of birth.

questions.subject: Polity
questions.q: The provision for 'Zero FIR' is contained in —
questions.e: A 'Zero FIR' can be registered at any police station regardless of jurisdiction under the BNSS, and must then be transferred to the police station having jurisdiction within 15 days.

questions.subject: Polity
questions.q: Trial in absentia of a proclaimed offender is provided under —
questions.e: Section 356 of the BNSS permits trial in absentia of a proclaimed offender, allowing courts to proceed when the accused absconds after the charge is framed.

questions.subject: Polity
questions.q: The office of the Comptroller and Auditor General is provided under which Article?
questions.e: Article 148 of the Constitution provides for the Comptroller and Auditor General of India, appointed by the President with a six-year term or until age 65.

questions.subject: Polity
questions.q: The committee recommending the NHRC chairperson's appointment is headed by —
questions.e: Under the Protection of Human Rights Act, 1993, the NHRC chairperson is appointed by the President on the recommendation of a committee headed by the Prime Minister.

questions.subject: Polity
questions.q: Who took charge as chairperson of the National Commission for Women in October 2024?
questions.e: Vijaya Rahatkar took charge as the chairperson of the National Commission for Women in October 2024, succeeding Rekha Sharma.

questions.subject: Polity
questions.q: Ajay Kumar was appointed chairman of the UPSC in —
questions.e: Former Defence Secretary Ajay Kumar was appointed chairman of the Union Public Service Commission in May 2025; he is a 1985-batch Kerala-cadre IAS officer.

questions.subject: Polity
questions.q: V. Narayanan took charge as ISRO chairman in —
questions.e: Distinguished scientist V. Narayanan, who led the LVM3 programme, took charge as ISRO chairman and Secretary, Department of Space, in January 2025, succeeding S. Somanath.

questions.subject: Polity
questions.q: Tuhin Kanta Pandey took charge as SEBI chairperson on —
questions.e: Tuhin Kanta Pandey, then Finance Secretary, took charge as SEBI chairperson on 1 March 2025 for a three-year term, succeeding Madhabi Puri Buch.

questions.subject: Polity
questions.q: Sanjay Malhotra is the ___ Governor of the Reserve Bank of India.
questions.e: Sanjay Malhotra is the 26th Governor of the Reserve Bank of India, succeeding Shaktikanta Das who served a six-year term from 2018 to 2024.

questions.subject: Polity
questions.q: CBI Director Praveen Sood's tenure was extended by one year in —
questions.e: The Appointments Committee of the Cabinet extended CBI Director Praveen Sood's tenure by one year in May 2025, beyond his original two-year term ending 24 May 2025.

questions.subject: Polity
questions.q: Rahul Navin was appointed Director of the Enforcement Directorate in —
questions.e: IRS officer Rahul Navin was appointed Director of the Enforcement Directorate in September 2024 after serving as acting chief since the tenure of S. K. Mishra ended.

questions.subject: Polity
questions.q: Who is the Director of the Intelligence Bureau (as of 2026)?
questions.e: Tapan Kumar Deka, a 1988-batch IPS officer of the Himachal Pradesh cadre, continues as Director of the Intelligence Bureau after extensions granted in 2024 and 2025.

questions.subject: Polity
questions.q: Who heads the Research and Analysis Wing (R&AW)?
questions.e: Ravi Sinha, a 1988-batch IPS officer of the Chhattisgarh cadre, took charge as Secretary (R&AW) in July 2023, heading India's external intelligence agency.

questions.subject: Polity
questions.q: Vikram Misri took charge as Foreign Secretary on —
questions.e: Vikram Misri, a 1989-batch IFS officer who was Deputy NSA, took charge as Foreign Secretary on 15 July 2024, succeeding Vinay Kwatra.

questions.subject: Polity
questions.q: T. V. Somanathan took charge as Cabinet Secretary on —
questions.e: T. V. Somanathan, a 1987-batch Tamil Nadu-cadre IAS officer, took over as Cabinet Secretary on 30 August 2024, succeeding Rajiv Gauba — the longest-serving Cabinet Secretary.

questions.subject: Polity
questions.q: Ajit Doval was reappointed National Security Adviser for a third term in —
questions.e: The government reappointed Ajit Doval as National Security Adviser for a third consecutive term in June 2024, also assigning him the additional charge of the Strategic Policy Group.

questions.subject: Polity
questions.q: Govind Mohan took charge as Union Home Secretary in —
questions.e: Govind Mohan, a 1989-batch Sikkim-cadre IAS officer, took charge as Union Home Secretary in August 2024, succeeding Ajay Kumar Bhalla.

questions.subject: Polity
questions.q: Rajesh Kumar Singh took charge as Defence Secretary on —
questions.e: Rajesh Kumar Singh, a 1989-batch Kerala-cadre IAS officer, took charge as Defence Secretary on 1 November 2024, succeeding Giridhar Aramane.

questions.subject: Polity
questions.q: The Attorney General of India holds office —
o: During the pleasure of the President
For a fixed term of five years
For a fixed term of six years
questions.e: Under Article 76, the Attorney General holds office during the pleasure of the President and has the right of audience in all courts in India.

questions.subject: Polity
questions.q: Who appoints the Attorney General of India?
questions.e: The Attorney General of India is appointed by the President under Article 76 and holds office during the pleasure of the President.

questions.subject: Polity
questions.q: Shaktikanta Das was appointed to which post in February 2025?
o: Principal Secretary-2 to the Prime Minister
questions.e: Former RBI Governor Shaktikanta Das was appointed Principal Secretary-2 to the Prime Minister in February 2025, serving alongside Principal Secretary P. K. Mishra.

questions.subject: Polity
questions.q: The Emergency in India was proclaimed on —
questions.e: The Emergency was proclaimed on the night of 25 June 1975 by President Fakhruddin Ali Ahmed on the advice of Prime Minister Indira Gandhi; 2025 marked its 50th anniversary.

questions.subject: Polity
questions.q: The 2024 Lok Sabha elections were conducted in how many phases?
questions.e: The 2024 general elections to the 18th Lok Sabha were held in seven phases from 19 April to 1 June 2024, with counting on 4 June 2024.

questions.subject: Polity
questions.q: How many women MPs were elected to the 18th Lok Sabha (2024)?
questions.e: Seventy-four women were elected to the 18th Lok Sabha in 2024 — about 13.6% of the House's strength, marginally lower than the 78 women MPs in the 17th Lok Sabha.

questions.subject: Polity
questions.q: Who became the Leader of the Opposition in the Lok Sabha in 2024?
questions.e: Rahul Gandhi became the Leader of the Opposition in the Lok Sabha in June 2024 — the first formally recognised LoP in a decade, after the post lay vacant through the 16th and 17th Lok Sabhas.

questions.subject: Polity
questions.q: Which 2025 Act allows bank account holders to name up to four nominees?
questions.e: The Banking Laws (Amendment) Act, 2025, which received assent in April 2025, makes 19 amendments across five laws including the RBI Act, Banking Regulation Act and SBI Act — notably allowing four nominees per bank account.

questions.subject: Polity
questions.q: The long-pending delimitation of constituencies will follow which Census?
questions.e: The next delimitation of Lok Sabha and Assembly constituencies — frozen since 1976 — will be carried out after the 2027 Census, the first Census conducted after 2026.

questions.subject: Polity
questions.q: The 'One Nation, One Election' Bill inserts which new Article for simultaneous polls?
questions.e: The Constitution (129th Amendment) Bill, 2024 inserts Article 82A to enable simultaneous elections to the Lok Sabha and State Assemblies.

questions.subject: Polity
questions.q: What is the approved outlay of the e-Courts Phase-III project?
questions.e: The e-Courts Phase-III project (2023–2027), approved with an outlay of ₹7,210 crore, aims to digitise court processes, enable virtual courts and create a unified national judicial data grid.

questions.subject: Polity
questions.q: Under the 2023 Act, the selection committee for the CEC and Election Commissioners is chaired by —
questions.e: Under the CEC and other ECs (Appointment, Conditions of Service and Term of Office) Act, 2023, the selection committee is chaired by the Prime Minister, with the Leader of Opposition in the Lok Sabha and a Union Cabinet Minister as members.

questions.subject: Economy
questions.q: The Budget 2025-26 raised the FDI limit in the insurance sector to —
questions.e: Budget 2025-26 raised the FDI cap in the insurance sector from 74% to 100%, a move aimed at deepening insurance penetration toward 'Insurance for All by 2047'.

questions.subject: Economy
questions.q: Budget 2025 raised the Kisan Credit Card loan limit to —
questions.e: Budget 2025 raised the Kisan Credit Card loan limit from ₹3 lakh to ₹5 lakh, benefiting over 7 crore farmers, fishermen and dairy farmers.

questions.subject: Schemes
questions.q: The PM Dhan-Dhaanya Krishi Yojana converges ___ existing schemes across ministries.
questions.e: The PM Dhan-Dhaanya Krishi Yojana converges 36 schemes of 11 ministries and departments, targeting 100 low-productivity districts in partnership with states.

questions.subject: Banking
questions.q: The Grameen Credit Score framework announced in Budget 2025 is aimed at —
questions.e: Budget 2025 announced a Grameen Credit Score framework to serve the credit needs of Self-Help Group members and rural borrowers through public-sector banks.

questions.subject: Economy
questions.q: The National Manufacturing Mission's mandate covers —
questions.e: The National Manufacturing Mission announced in Budget 2025 has a mandate covering small, medium and large industries to further 'Make in India'.

questions.subject: Economy
questions.q: Budget 2025 raised MSME investment limits by —
questions.e: Budget 2025 raised the MSME investment limits by 2.5 times and turnover limits by 2 times, widening the coverage of MSME benefits.

questions.subject: Economy
questions.q: Under Budget 2025's new tax regime, the nil-tax slab was raised to —
questions.e: Budget 2025 raised the nil-tax slab to ₹4 lakh and, with the enhanced rebate, made annual income up to ₹12 lakh effectively tax-free under the new regime.

questions.subject: Economy
questions.q: Budget 2025 proposed how many customs tariff rates?
questions.e: Budget 2025 proposed rationalising the customs tariff structure to seven rates (including zero), removing seven tariff rates to simplify the regime.

questions.subject: Economy
questions.q: The India-EFTA Trade and Economic Partnership Agreement came into force on —
questions.e: The India-EFTA Trade and Economic Partnership Agreement — with Iceland, Liechtenstein, Norway and Switzerland — came into force on 1 October 2025, with a $100-billion investment commitment.

questions.subject: International
questions.q: Which country is NOT a member of the European Free Trade Association (EFTA)?
questions.e: EFTA comprises Iceland, Liechtenstein, Norway and Switzerland; Sweden is a European Union member and not part of EFTA.

questions.subject: International
questions.q: 'Mission 500' in India-US ties refers to —
questions.e: The February 2025 Modi-Trump joint statement launched 'Mission 500', targeting $500 billion in bilateral India-US trade by 2030.

questions.subject: Schemes
questions.q: The PM MUDRA Yojana completed 10 years in —
questions.e: The Pradhan Mantri MUDRA Yojana, launched in April 2015 to fund micro-enterprises, completed 10 years in April 2025 with over 52 crore loans sanctioned cumulatively.

questions.subject: Banking
questions.q: The 'Tarun Plus' category under MUDRA provides loans up to —
questions.e: Budget 2024 introduced the 'Tarun Plus' category under MUDRA for entrepreneurs who have repaid earlier Tarun loans, offering up to ₹20 lakh.

questions.subject: Economy
questions.q: The Unified Pension Scheme assures a pension of ___ of average basic pay.
questions.e: The Unified Pension Scheme, effective 1 April 2025, assures central government employees a pension of 50% of the average basic pay over the last 12 months before retirement.

questions.subject: Banking
questions.q: NPS Vatsalya is a pension scheme for —
questions.e: NPS Vatsalya, launched in September 2024, is a pension scheme for minors, allowing parents and guardians to build a retirement corpus for children.

questions.subject: Banking
questions.q: The Reserve Bank of India completed 90 years in —
questions.e: The Reserve Bank of India, established on 1 April 1935 under the RBI Act, 1934, completed 90 years in 2025.

questions.subject: Economy
questions.q: The National Critical Mineral Mission spans the period —
questions.e: The National Critical Mineral Mission, approved in January 2025 with a ₹34,300-crore outlay, spans seven financial years from 2025-26 to 2031-32.

questions.subject: Economy
questions.q: The Maritime Development Fund announced in Budget 2025 will primarily finance —
questions.e: The ₹25,000-crore Maritime Development Fund will finance shipbuilding, port modernisation and related maritime infrastructure, with up to 49% government contribution.

questions.subject: SciTech
questions.q: The Nuclear Energy Mission aims to operationalise at least ___ indigenous SMRs by 2033. ⚠verify
questions.e: The Budget 2025 speech set a goal of at least five indigenously developed small modular reactors ('Bharat SMRs') operational by 2033. ⚠verify

questions.subject: SciTech
questions.q: In the nuclear sector, 'SMR' stands for —
questions.e: SMR stands for Small Modular Reactor — factory-built compact nuclear reactors; the Budget 2025 mission aims to develop indigenous Bharat SMRs.

questions.subject: Schemes
questions.q: The Jal Jeevan Mission was extended till —
questions.e: Budget 2025 extended the Jal Jeevan Mission till 2028 with an enhanced outlay, shifting focus to operation and maintenance of rural tap-water infrastructure.

questions.subject: Schemes
questions.q: What is the approved outlay of the Digital Agriculture Mission?
questions.e: The Union Cabinet approved the Digital Agriculture Mission in September 2024 with an outlay of ₹2,817 crore, built on Agri Stack, Krishi DSS and soil-profile mapping.

questions.subject: SciTech
questions.q: The primary goal of 'Mission Mausam' is to —
o: Improve weather forecasting and climate services
questions.e: Mission Mausam (₹2,000 crore) aims to make India 'weather-ready' through high-resolution observations, AI-based modelling and better forecasts down to the panchayat level.

questions.subject: SciTech
questions.q: 'Mission Mausam' is implemented by —
questions.e: Mission Mausam is implemented by the Ministry of Earth Sciences through the IMD, the Indian Institute of Tropical Meteorology and the NCMRWF.

questions.subject: Schemes
questions.q: The Vibrant Villages Programme-II announced in Budget 2025 covers —
questions.e: Budget 2025 announced the Vibrant Villages Programme-II for strategic border villages, extending the 2023 programme beyond the northern border to all international land borders.

questions.subject: Economy
questions.q: India is the world's ___ largest coal producer.
questions.e: India is the world's second-largest coal producer after China; domestic production crossed 1 billion tonnes for the first time in FY 2024-25.

questions.subject: Environment
questions.q: The largest feedstock for India's ethanol blending programme is —
questions.e: Sugarcane (juice, syrup and molasses) remains the dominant feedstock for India's ethanol blending programme, supplemented by maize and surplus rice.

questions.subject: SciTech
questions.q: The Tata-PSMC semiconductor fab at Dholera will have a monthly capacity of — ⚠verify
questions.e: The Dholera fab is designed for about 50,000 wafer starts per month, manufacturing power-management and display-driver chips on mature nodes. ⚠verify

questions.subject: SciTech
questions.q: Tata Semiconductor's chip assembly and test (OSAT) facility is coming up in —
questions.e: Tata Semiconductor's ₹27,000-crore assembly and test (OSAT) facility is coming up at Jagiroad, Morigaon district, Assam.

questions.subject: SciTech
questions.q: Micron's Sanand semiconductor facility involves a total investment of —
questions.e: Micron's semiconductor assembly and test facility at Sanand, Gujarat, involves a total investment of $2.75 billion, the largest under the India Semiconductor Mission so far.

questions.subject: SciTech
questions.q: The India Semiconductor Mission functions under —
questions.e: The India Semiconductor Mission operates under the Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology through the Digital India Corporation.

questions.subject: Environment
questions.q: What is the approved outlay of the National Green Hydrogen Mission?
questions.e: The National Green Hydrogen Mission, approved in January 2023, has an outlay of ₹19,744 crore till FY 2029-30, targeting 5 MMT annual green hydrogen capacity by 2030.

questions.subject: Environment
questions.q: Green hydrogen is produced using —
questions.e: Green hydrogen is hydrogen produced by electrolysing water using renewable electricity, yielding no carbon emissions; grey hydrogen comes from natural gas reforming.

questions.subject: Schemes
questions.q: The PM Surya Ghar: Muft Bijli Yojana targets —
questions.e: The PM Surya Ghar: Muft Bijli Yojana, launched in February 2024, targets rooftop solar installations for 1 crore households with subsidies up to ₹78,000.

questions.subject: Economy
questions.q: The Production Linked Incentive (PLI) scheme covers how many sectors?
questions.e: The Production Linked Incentive scheme now covers 14 sectors — from mobile manufacturing and pharma to drones, textiles and white goods — with an outlay of about ₹1.97 lakh crore.

questions.subject: Economy
questions.q: The Open Network for Digital Commerce (ONDC) is an initiative of —
questions.e: The Open Network for Digital Commerce (ONDC) is a DPIIT initiative under the Commerce Ministry to democratise e-commerce through open interoperable networks.

questions.subject: Banking
questions.q: The Account Aggregator framework is regulated by —
questions.e: The Account Aggregator framework — enabling consent-based sharing of financial data — is regulated by the Reserve Bank of India.

questions.subject: Banking
questions.q: India's retail central bank digital currency (e-rupee) pilot was launched in —
questions.e: The RBI launched the retail pilot of the e-rupee (CBDC-R) in December 2022, starting with Mumbai, Delhi, Bengaluru and Bhubaneswar.

questions.subject: Banking
questions.q: 'Bima Sugam' is —
questions.e: Bima Sugam is IRDAI's proposed digital marketplace — a 'UPI-like' one-stop platform for buying insurance, settling claims and servicing policies.

questions.subject: Places
questions.q: The Chenab rail bridge, inaugurated in June 2025, is the —
questions.e: The Chenab rail bridge — at 359 metres above the riverbed, the world's highest railway arch bridge — was inaugurated by PM Modi on 6 June 2025 as part of the USBRL project.

questions.subject: Places
questions.q: The USBRL rail project connects —
questions.e: The Udhampur-Srinagar-Baramulla Rail Link (USBRL), a 272-km all-weather line built over nearly three decades, was fully completed in 2025.

questions.subject: SciTech
questions.q: The Katra–Srinagar Vande Bharat Express is operated by —
questions.e: The Katra–Srinagar Vande Bharat, flagged off in June 2025 over the USBRL alignment, is operated by Northern Railway, which also maintains the Chenab and Anji Khad bridges.

questions.subject: Places
questions.q: The Anji Khad bridge is India's first —
questions.e: The Anji Khad bridge on the USBRL alignment is India's first cable-stayed railway bridge, with a 331-metre-high pylon.

questions.subject: Places
questions.q: The Z-Morh tunnel, inaugurated in January 2025, is located in —
questions.e: PM Modi inaugurated the Z-Morh tunnel in Ganderbal, Jammu and Kashmir, on 13 January 2025, ensuring all-weather connectivity to Sonamarg.

questions.subject: SciTech
questions.q: 'Kavach', the indigenous Automatic Train Protection system, was developed by —
questions.e: Kavach was developed by the Research Designs and Standards Organisation (RDSO), the Railways' R&D arm, and is being rolled out across the network after successful trials.

questions.subject: Banking
questions.q: RBI's PRAVAAH portal is meant for —
questions.e: RBI's PRAVAAH (Platform for Regulatory Application, Validation and Authorisation), launched in May 2024, is a centralised portal for entities to seek regulatory approvals from the RBI.

questions.subject: Banking
questions.q: RBI's UDGAM portal helps citizens with —
questions.e: RBI's UDGAM (Unclaimed Deposits – Gateway to Access inforMation) portal, launched in 2023, helps citizens trace unclaimed deposits across banks.

questions.subject: Economy
questions.q: DPIIT functions under the —
questions.e: The Department for Promotion of Industry and Internal Trade (DPIIT) is part of the Ministry of Commerce and Industry and anchors initiatives like ONDC, Startup India and the PLI schemes.

questions.subject: Economy
questions.q: The Goods and Services Tax (GST) completed 8 years of implementation on —
questions.e: GST was launched on 1 July 2017; it completed eight years on 1 July 2025, with the 56th GST Council meeting in September 2025 ushering in next-generation rate rationalisation.

questions.subject: SciTech
questions.q: 'Amrit Bharat' trains introduced by Indian Railways are —
o: Non-AC trains with upgraded amenities for common passengers
questions.e: Amrit Bharat trains are non-AC push-pull services with upgraded second-class, sleeper and general coaches aimed at migrant workers and common passengers.

questions.subject: Defence
questions.q: The AMCA is being developed as a ___ generation fighter aircraft.
questions.e: The Advanced Medium Combat Aircraft (AMCA) is India's indigenous fifth-generation stealth fighter; the CCS approved its execution model with industry partnership in May 2025.

questions.subject: Defence
questions.q: India's October 2024 MQ-9B Predator drone deal with the US is worth —
questions.e: India signed a $3.5-billion deal in October 2024 for 31 MQ-9B Predator drones (16 SkyGuardian, 15 SeaGuardian) from the US, split across the three services.

questions.subject: Defence
questions.q: INS Vaghsheer is —
o: The first ASW Shallow Water Craft
The sixth and last Scorpene-class submarine
questions.e: INS Vaghsheer is the sixth and final Kalvari (Scorpene)-class submarine built at Mazagon Dock under Project 75, commissioned in January 2025.

questions.subject: Defence
questions.q: INS Udaygiri and INS Himgiri were commissioned in —
questions.e: INS Udaygiri and INS Himgiri — the second and third Nilgiri-class (Project 17A) stealth frigates — were commissioned together at Visakhapatnam on 26 August 2025.

questions.subject: Defence
questions.q: INS Arnala, the first ASW Shallow Water Craft, was commissioned in —
questions.e: INS Arnala, the first of the 16 Anti-Submarine Warfare Shallow Water Craft, was commissioned on 18 June 2025 at Visakhapatnam.

questions.subject: Defence
questions.q: India's two defence industrial corridors are located in —
questions.e: India's two defence industrial corridors — announced in 2018-19 — are in Uttar Pradesh (6 nodes) and Tamil Nadu (5 nodes), anchoring domestic defence manufacturing.

questions.subject: Defence
questions.q: INS Tamal, the last imported warship, was commissioned in —
questions.e: INS Tamal, the last imported warship (a Talwar-class stealth frigate built in Russia), was commissioned in July 2025 at Kaliningrad.

questions.subject: Defence
questions.q: DRDO's Nag Mk-2 anti-tank missile trials were conducted in —
questions.e: DRDO successfully conducted field trials of the Nag Mk-2, an indigenously developed third-generation anti-tank guided missile, in January 2025 at Pokhran.

questions.subject: Defence
questions.q: India's defence exports in FY 2024-25 stood at —
questions.e: India's defence exports hit a record ₹23,622 crore in FY 2024-25, with the government targeting ₹50,000 crore by 2029.

questions.subject: Defence
questions.q: The March 2025 Myanmar earthquake's epicentre was near — ⚠verify
questions.e: The 7.7-magnitude earthquake of 28 March 2025 had its epicentre in the Sagaing region near Mandalay, Myanmar; India launched Operation Brahma for relief. ⚠verify

questions.subject: Defence
questions.q: Operation Sindhu (June 2025) evacuated Indian nationals from —
questions.e: Operation Sindhu was launched in June 2025 to evacuate Indian nationals from Iran amid the Iran-Israel conflict, using special flights via Armenia and Turkmenistan.

questions.subject: Defence
questions.q: India-China disengagement at Depsang and Demchok was completed in —
questions.e: India and China completed disengagement at Depsang and Demchok in eastern Ladakh in October 2024, ending the four-year military standoff that began in 2020.

questions.subject: Defence
questions.q: The Kailash Mansarovar Yatra resumed in 2025 after a gap of —
questions.e: The Kailash Mansarovar Yatra resumed in 2025 after a five-year gap (suspended since 2020), with pilgrims travelling via the Lipulekh and Nathu La routes.

questions.subject: Defence
questions.q: The Tata-Airbus C-295 military aircraft plant is located at —
questions.e: India's first private military aircraft manufacturing plant — the Tata-Airbus C-295 facility — was inaugurated at Vadodara, Gujarat, in October 2024.

questions.subject: Defence
questions.q: 'Pinaka' is an indigenous —
questions.e: Pinaka is DRDO's indigenous multi-barrel rocket launcher (214mm), with extended-range versions reaching 75 km; it has been exported to Armenia.

questions.subject: Defence
questions.q: India delivered the first BrahMos missiles to the Philippines in —
questions.e: India delivered the first batch of BrahMos supersonic cruise missiles to the Philippines in April 2024 under a $375-million deal signed in 2022.

questions.subject: Defence
questions.q: JIMEX is the bilateral naval exercise between India and —
questions.e: JIMEX is the bilateral maritime exercise between India and Japan; its 2024 edition was held in the Bay of Bengal.

questions.subject: Defence
questions.q: The India-Japan army exercise 'Dharma Guardian' focuses on —
questions.e: Dharma Guardian, the annual India-Japan bilateral army exercise, focuses on counter-terrorism operations and UN peacekeeping in urban and semi-urban terrain.

questions.subject: Defence
questions.q: The 2025 edition of 'Tiger Triumph' was held off the coast of —
questions.e: Tiger Triumph 2025, the fourth edition of the India-US tri-services HADR exercise, was conducted off Visakhapatnam in April 2025.

questions.subject: Defence
questions.q: 'Vajra Prahar' is the special forces exercise between India and —
questions.e: Vajra Prahar is the India-US joint special forces exercise, conducted alternately in India and the United States.

questions.subject: Defence
questions.q: The multilateral naval exercise 'La Perouse' is led by —
questions.e: La Perouse is a France-led multilateral naval exercise; India participated with its P-8I aircraft in the 2025 edition in the Malacca Strait region.

questions.subject: Defence
questions.q: 'Desert Knight' is the air exercise involving —
questions.e: Desert Knight is a trilateral air exercise involving India, France and the UAE, first held in January 2024 over the Arabian Sea.

questions.subject: Defence
questions.q: 'Garuda Shakti' is a ___ exercise.
questions.e: Garuda Shakti is the bilateral special forces exercise between India and Indonesia, held since 2012, focusing on counter-terrorism.

questions.subject: Defence
questions.q: 'Mitra Shakti' is the army exercise between India and —
questions.e: Mitra Shakti is the annual bilateral army exercise between India and Sri Lanka, focused on counter-insurgency and counter-terrorism.

questions.subject: Defence
questions.q: 'Sampriti' is the army exercise between India and —
questions.e: Sampriti is the bilateral army exercise between India and Bangladesh, hosted alternately by the two countries.

questions.subject: Defence
questions.q: 'Bold Kurukshetra' is the army exercise between India and —
questions.e: Exercise Bold Kurukshetra is the bilateral army exercise between India and Singapore, involving mechanised forces.

questions.subject: Defence
questions.q: The India-Maldives exercise 'Ekuverin' has been conducted since —
questions.e: Ekuverin, the bilateral military exercise between India and the Maldives, has been held since 2009, alternately in the two countries.

questions.subject: Defence
questions.q: 'Surya Kiran' is the army exercise between India and —
questions.e: Surya Kiran is the bilateral army exercise between India and Nepal, conducted alternately in the two countries.

questions.subject: Defence
questions.q: 'Khanjar' is the special forces exercise between India and —
questions.e: Khanjar is the bilateral special forces exercise between India and Kyrgyzstan, focused on counter-terrorism in mountainous terrain.

questions.subject: Defence
questions.q: 'Lamitye' is the exercise between India and —
questions.e: Lamitye is the bilateral army exercise between India and Seychelles, held since 2001.

questions.subject: Defence
questions.q: 'Ajeya Warrior' is the army exercise between India and —
questions.e: Ajeya Warrior is the bilateral army exercise between India and the United Kingdom, focused on counter-terrorism operations.

questions.subject: Defence
questions.q: The India-UK naval exercise 'Konkan' began in —
questions.e: Konkan, the bilateral naval exercise between India and the United Kingdom, has been conducted since 2004.

questions.subject: Defence
questions.q: 'Indra' is the tri-services exercise between India and —
questions.e: Indra is the bilateral tri-services exercise between India and Russia, held alternately in the two countries.

questions.subject: Defence
questions.q: 'Zayed Talwar' is the naval exercise between India and —
questions.e: Zayed Talwar is the bilateral naval exercise between India and the UAE, aimed at enhancing maritime cooperation in the Gulf.

questions.q: The 20th UNESCO ICH session (Dec 2025) was held at —

questions.subject: Culture
questions.q: The 2025 Maha Kumbh was held at —
questions.e: The Maha Kumbh Mela was held at Prayagraj in January–February 2025, with a 'Kalagram' cultural zone in the tent city.

questions.subject: Culture
questions.q: 'Vande Mataram' is India's —
questions.e: 'Vande Mataram' — India's national song — completed 150 years in November 2025, marked by year-long celebrations.

questions.subject: Culture
questions.q: Gyan Bharatam will digitise —
questions.e: The Gyan Bharatam portal (launched 12 September 2025) aims to digitise India's ancient manuscripts.

questions.subject: Culture
questions.q: 2025 was the 300th birth anniversary of —
questions.e: 2025 marked the 300th birth anniversary of Ahilyabai Holkar, celebrated with a grand function in Bhopal.

questions.subject: Culture
questions.q: National Unity Day honours —
questions.e: National Unity Day (31 October) honours Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel; 2025 marked his 150th birth year.

questions.subject: Sports
questions.q: The 2025 Women's ODI World Cup was the ___ edition.
questions.e: The 2025 Women's ODI World Cup — won by India — was the 13th edition of the tournament.

questions.subject: Sports
questions.q: The Asian Games are held every —
questions.e: The Asian Games are held every four years; Aichi-Nagoya (Japan) hosts the 20th edition in 2026.

questions.subject: Sports
questions.q: Glasgow stepped in for the 2026 CWG after ___ withdrew.
questions.e: Glasgow stepped in to host the scaled-down 2026 Commonwealth Games after Victoria, Australia, withdrew.

questions.subject: Sports
questions.q: The 2030 FIFA World Cup will be hosted by —
questions.e: The 2030 FIFA World Cup will be hosted by Spain, Portugal and Morocco (with centenary matches in South America).

questions.subject: Sports
questions.q: The 2026 Men's T20 World Cup will be the ___ edition.
questions.e: The 2026 Men's T20 World Cup (India and Sri Lanka) will be the 10th edition.

questions.subject: Sports
questions.q: The 2030 FIFA World Cup centenary matches will be played in —
questions.e: The 2030 FIFA World Cup (Spain, Portugal, Morocco) will stage centenary matches in South America, 100 years after Uruguay 1930.

questions.subject: Culture
questions.q: The December 2025 ICH session was the ___ session.
questions.e: The 20th session of UNESCO's ICH Intergovernmental Committee was held at Delhi's Red Fort in December 2025 — India's first hosting.

questions.subject: Schemes
questions.q: The Viksit Bharat Rozgar Yojana (Employment Linked Incentive scheme), approved on 1 July 2025, carries a total outlay of —
questions.e: The Union Cabinet approved the Viksit Bharat Rozgar Yojana on 1 July 2025 with an outlay of ₹99,446 crore, targeting the creation of over 3.5 crore jobs in two years.

questions.subject: Schemes
questions.q: Under the Viksit Bharat Rozgar Yojana, a first-time employee registered with EPFO receives an incentive of up to —
questions.e: First-time employees earning up to ₹1 lakh per month get an incentive of up to ₹15,000 paid in two instalments (after 6 and 12 months of service), while employers get up to ₹3,000 per month per additional employee for two years.

questions.subject: Schemes
questions.q: The PM Dhan Dhanya Krishi Yojana, announced in the Union Budget 2025-26, targets how many districts?
questions.e: The PM Dhan Dhanya Krishi Yojana converges 36 schemes across 11 departments to raise productivity in 100 low-performing districts, benefiting about 1.7 crore farmers.

questions.subject: Schemes
questions.q: SWAMIH Fund 2, announced in Budget 2025-26, was created with a corpus of ₹15,000 crore for —
questions.e: SWAMIH Fund 2 (₹15,000 crore) extends the 2019 SWAMIH Fund model to deliver stalled residential projects; the first fund aimed at completing nearly 4.6 lakh stressed housing units.

questions.subject: Schemes
questions.q: The Biopharma SHAKTI scheme announced in Budget 2026-27 has an outlay of ₹10,000 crore over five years to —
o: make India a global hub for biologics and biosimilars
questions.e: Biopharma SHAKTI, announced in the Union Budget 2026-27 with ₹10,000 crore over five years, aims to position India as a global hub for biologics, biosimilars and bio-manufacturing.

questions.subject: Schemes
questions.q: The SME Growth Fund proposed in the Union Budget 2026-27 has a corpus of —
questions.e: Budget 2026-27 proposed a ₹10,000 crore SME Growth Fund to create future champions among micro, small and medium enterprises, alongside 'Corporate Mitras' in Tier-II and Tier-III towns.

questions.subject: Schemes
questions.q: India Semiconductor Mission 2.0, announced in Budget 2026-27, focuses primarily on —
questions.e: ISM 2.0, launched in Budget 2026-27, expands the mission beyond fabs into semiconductor equipment and materials, building on ISM 1.0's fab and OSAT projects at Dholera, Sanand and Morigaon.

questions.subject: Schemes
questions.q: Under the PM Surya Ghar Muft Bijli Yojana, the subsidy for a 2 kW rooftop solar installation is —
questions.e: PM Surya Ghar (launched February 2024, outlay ₹75,021 crore) gives ₹30,000 for 1 kW, ₹60,000 for 2 kW and ₹78,000 for 3 kW or higher, targeting 1 crore households with 300 free units per month.

questions.subject: Schemes
questions.q: In October 2024, Ayushman Bharat PM-JAY coverage was extended to —
o: all senior citizens aged 70 and above, irrespective of income
only BPL families in urban areas
questions.e: The October 2024 expansion brought every senior citizen aged 70+ under PM-JAY regardless of income, with a separate ₹5 lakh annual top-up cover on a family basis.

questions.subject: Schemes
questions.q: The Unified Pension Scheme (UPS), effective 1 April 2025, assures a pension of —
o: 50% of the average basic pay of the last 12 months
questions.e: Notified in January 2025 for central government employees, UPS assures 50% of the average basic pay of the last 12 months (after 25 years of service), a 60% family pension, and a minimum pension of ₹10,000 per month.

questions.subject: Schemes
questions.q: The 8th Central Pay Commission was approved by the Union Cabinet in —
questions.e: The Cabinet approved the constitution of the 8th Central Pay Commission on 16 January 2025; its recommendations will revise pay and pensions of central government employees.

questions.subject: Schemes
questions.q: Under the PM Internship Scheme, an intern receives a monthly assistance of —
questions.e: Announced in Budget 2024-25, the PM Internship Scheme targets 1 crore youth in top 500 companies over five years, paying ₹5,000 per month (₹4,500 from the government and ₹500 from CSR) plus a ₹6,000 one-time grant.

questions.subject: Schemes
questions.q: The National Mission on Edible Oils–Oilseeds (NMEO-Oilseeds), approved in October 2024, has a financial outlay of —
questions.e: NMEO-Oilseeds (₹10,103 crore for 2024-25 to 2030-31) aims to raise domestic oilseed production to 69.7 million tonnes and cut India's heavy dependence on imported edible oils.

questions.subject: Schemes
questions.q: Mission Mausam, approved in September 2024 with an outlay of ₹2,000 crore, is implemented by —
questions.e: Mission Mausam (₹2,000 crore) under the Ministry of Earth Sciences upgrades weather and climate forecasting with advanced radars, satellites and high-performance computing.

questions.subject: Schemes
questions.q: The PM E-DRIVE scheme (September 2024, ₹10,900 crore) replaced which earlier scheme?
questions.e: PM E-DRIVE (₹10,900 crore, two years) succeeded the FAME scheme, subsidising e-two-wheelers, e-three-wheelers, e-buses, e-ambulances and charging infrastructure.

questions.subject: Schemes
questions.q: The 'Vigyan Dhara' scheme of the Department of Science and Technology, approved in August 2024, has an outlay of —
questions.e: Vigyan Dhara (₹10,579 crore for 2021-26) merged several DST schemes into three components: S&T capacity building, research and innovation, and technology deployment.

questions.subject: Schemes
questions.q: The BioE3 (Biotechnology for Economy, Environment and Employment) policy, approved in August 2024, carries an outlay of —
questions.e: The BioE3 policy (₹9,197 crore) promotes high-performance biomanufacturing across six themes including bio-based chemicals, smart proteins and climate-resilient agriculture.

questions.subject: Schemes
questions.q: The National Quantum Mission, approved in 2023, has a total outlay of —
questions.e: The National Quantum Mission (₹6,003.65 crore for 2023-31) aims to build quantum computers of 50-1000 qubits, satellite-based quantum communication and quantum materials within eight years.

questions.subject: Schemes
questions.q: The National Critical Mineral Mission, approved in January 2025, envisages a government outlay of —
o: ₹16,300 crore plus ₹18,000 crore expected PSU investment
questions.e: The National Critical Mineral Mission (₹16,300 crore over seven years, plus ~₹18,000 crore expected from PSUs) secures lithium, cobalt, rare earths and other critical minerals for clean energy and electronics.

questions.subject: Schemes
questions.q: The six-year 'Mission for Aatmanirbharta in Pulses', announced in Budget 2025-26, focuses especially on —
questions.e: Budget 2025-26 launched a six-year mission for self-sufficiency in pulses with special focus on tur, urad and masoor, with assured procurement through NAFED and NCCF.

questions.subject: Schemes
questions.q: The Makhana Board announced in Budget 2025-26 is to be set up in —
questions.e: Budget 2025-26 announced a Makhana Board in Bihar to improve production, processing and marketing of fox nuts, of which Bihar is the dominant producer.

questions.subject: Schemes
questions.q: Budget 2025-26 announced a National Institute of Food Technology, Entrepreneurship and Management in —
questions.e: Alongside the Makhana Board, Budget 2025-26 announced a National Institute of Food Technology, Entrepreneurship and Management in Bihar to boost food processing in the eastern region.

questions.subject: Schemes
questions.q: The Jal Jeevan Mission, which aimed at tap connections to every rural household, was extended in Budget 2025-26 up to —
questions.e: Budget 2025-26 extended the Jal Jeevan Mission to 2028 with an enhanced outlay, shifting emphasis to the quality of water supply and operation-and-maintenance of rural tap connections.

questions.subject: Schemes
questions.q: The Bharatiya Bhasha Pustak Scheme, announced in Budget 2025-26, provides —
o: digital Indian-language books for school and higher education
questions.e: The Bharatiya Bhasha Pustak Scheme provides digital-form Indian-language books for school and higher education, supporting learning in the mother tongue under NEP 2020.

questions.subject: Schemes
questions.q: Budget 2025-26 announced the setting up of 50,000 Atal Tinkering Labs in government schools over —
questions.e: Budget 2025-26 proposed 50,000 Atal Tinkering Labs in government schools over the next five years to foster curiosity, creativity and STEM skills.

questions.subject: Schemes
questions.q: Budget 2025-26 announced day-care cancer centres in all district hospitals within —
questions.e: Budget 2025-26 committed to establishing day-care cancer centres in all district hospitals over three years, alongside customs-duty exemption on 36 life-saving drugs.

questions.subject: Schemes
questions.q: The 'Grameen Credit Score' framework announced in Budget 2025-26 is meant for —
o: Self-Help Group members and rural borrowers
questions.e: Budget 2025-26 proposed a Grameen Credit Score framework to serve the credit needs of Self-Help Group members and people in rural areas, improving formal credit access.

questions.subject: Schemes
questions.q: In its 2025-26 restructuring, PM SVANidhi added which new feature for street vendors? ⚠verify
questions.e: The restructured PM SVANidhi (Budget 2025-26) raised loan slabs and added a UPI-linked RuPay credit card for street vendors who repay on time. ⚠verify

questions.subject: Schemes
questions.q: The Lakhpati Didi initiative aims to make how many women 'lakhpati' through Self-Help Groups?
questions.e: The Lakhpati Didi target was raised from 2 crore to 3 crore women — each earning at least ₹1 lakh per year through diversified Self-Help Group livelihoods.

questions.subject: Schemes
questions.q: The 19th instalment of PM-KISAN was released in February 2025 from —
questions.e: Prime Minister Modi released the 19th PM-KISAN instalment (over ₹22,000 crore to 9.8 crore farmers) from Bhagalpur, Bihar, in February 2025.

questions.subject: Schemes
questions.q: The Namo Drone Didi scheme aims to provide drones to —
questions.e: Namo Drone Didi supplies drones to 15,000 women Self-Help Groups for rental-based agricultural services like fertiliser and pesticide spraying.

questions.subject: Schemes
questions.q: The PM Janjatiya Unnat Gram Abhiyan (September 2024), with an outlay of ₹79,156 crore, covers —
o: tribal districts in the Northeast only
63,000 tribal villages benefiting about 5 crore tribals
questions.e: Approved in September 2024 (₹79,156 crore), the PM Janjatiya Unnat Gram Abhiyan saturates 63,000 tribal-majority villages with 25 interventions across 17 ministries, benefiting about 5 crore tribal people.

questions.subject: Schemes
questions.q: PM-JANMAN (Pradhan Mantri Janjati Adivasi Nyaya Maha Abhiyan), launched in November 2023, targets —
questions.e: PM-JANMAN (₹24,104 crore) focuses on the 75 Particularly Vulnerable Tribal Groups with housing, roads, piped water, mobile connectivity and education in three years.

questions.subject: Schemes
questions.q: The outlay for the Electronics Components Manufacturing Scheme was raised in Budget 2026-27 to —
questions.e: Budget 2026-27 sharply raised the Electronics Components Manufacturing Scheme outlay to ₹40,000 crore to deepen domestic electronics supply chains.

questions.subject: Schemes
questions.q: Which of the following was NOT announced in the Union Budget 2026-27?
o: A National Sports University in every state
questions.e: Budget 2026-27 announced Biopharma SHAKTI (₹10,000 crore), the SME Growth Fund (₹10,000 crore) and ISM 2.0 — but no scheme for a sports university in every state.

questions.subject: Banking
questions.q: In its August 2026 monetary policy, the RBI kept the repo rate unchanged at 5.25% — this was the —
questions.e: The RBI's August 2026 policy kept the repo rate at 5.25% with a 5:1 vote — the fourth straight pause after the last 25 bps cut in December 2025.

questions.subject: Banking
questions.q: As of the August 2026 RBI policy, the Standing Deposit Facility rate stood at —
questions.e: In August 2026 the SDF stayed at 5.00% while the Marginal Standing Facility and Bank Rate stayed at 5.50%, with the repo rate at 5.25%.

questions.subject: Banking
questions.q: The RBI retained which policy stance in its August 2026 monetary policy review?
questions.e: The RBI retained the 'neutral' stance in August 2026, keeping flexibility to respond to growth and inflation data.

questions.subject: Banking
questions.q: The RBI's next monetary policy meeting after August 2026 was scheduled for —
questions.e: After the August 2026 review, the RBI's next MPC meeting was scheduled for 5–7 October 2026.

questions.subject: Banking
questions.q: The last repo rate cut before the August 2026 pause was in —
questions.e: The RBI last cut the repo rate by 25 bps in December 2025 (to 5.25%), completing 125 bps of cuts during 2025 before the four consecutive pauses.

questions.subject: Banking
questions.q: UPI transactions in August 2026 touched a record —
questions.e: NPCI data showed August 2026 as a record month: 24.51 billion UPI transactions worth ₹29.82 lakh crore, about 791 million transactions per day.

questions.subject: Banking
questions.q: How many banks were live on UPI as of August 2026?
questions.e: NPCI reported 752 banks live on UPI in August 2026, underlining the network's deep reach.

questions.subject: Banking
questions.q: From 15 October 2026, UPI merchant discount rate (MDR) applies to person-to-merchant payments above —
questions.e: From 15 October 2026, UPI P2M payments above ₹2,000 carry a 0.4% MDR (capped) paid by merchants; person-to-person payments stay free.

questions.subject: Banking
questions.q: For essential services like railways, telecom, fuel and insurance, the flat UPI fee above ₹2,000 from October 2026 is —
questions.e: Essential services (railways, telecom, fuel, insurance) face a flat ₹5 fee per UPI transaction above ₹2,000 from October 2026, lower than the general 0.4% MDR.

questions.subject: Banking
questions.q: The Reserve Bank of India was established on —
questions.e: The RBI was established on 1 April 1935 under the RBI Act, 1934, and was nationalised on 1 January 1949; its headquarters is in Mumbai.

questions.subject: Banking
questions.q: The State Bank of India traces its origin to —
questions.e: SBI's lineage runs through the Bank of Bengal (1806), one of the three presidency banks merged in 1921 to form the Imperial Bank of India, renamed SBI in 1955.

questions.subject: Banking
questions.q: The first round of bank nationalisation in India (14 banks) took place on —
questions.e: Fourteen major banks were nationalised on 19 July 1969; six more followed on 15 April 1980.

questions.subject: Banking
questions.q: The deposit insurance cover per depositor per bank, raised in 2021, is —
questions.e: DICGC (a wholly owned RBI subsidiary) cover was raised from ₹1 lakh to ₹5 lakh per depositor per bank in 2021.

questions.subject: Banking
questions.q: The RBI's retail CBDC (e₹-R) pilot was launched on —
questions.e: The wholesale e-rupee pilot began on 31 October 2022 and the retail e-rupee (e₹-R) pilot on 1 December 2022.

questions.subject: Banking
questions.q: UPI was launched in 2016 by —
questions.e: The Unified Payments Interface was launched in 2016 by the National Payments Corporation of India.

questions.subject: Banking
questions.q: India's first payments bank to begin operations was —
questions.e: Airtel Payments Bank was the first payments bank to start operations (November 2016); Paytm Payments Bank's operations were wound down on RBI orders in 2024.

questions.subject: Banking
questions.q: Who took charge as SEBI chairperson in March 2025?
questions.e: Tuhin Kanta Pandey took charge as SEBI chairperson on 1 March 2025 for a three-year term; SEBI was set up in 1988 and given statutory powers in 1992.

questions.subject: Banking
questions.q: NABARD was established on 12 July 1982 on the recommendation of —
questions.e: NABARD was set up on 12 July 1982 following the Sivaraman Committee's recommendation, taking over RBI's agricultural credit functions; it is headquartered in Mumbai.

questions.subject: Banking
questions.q: Under priority sector lending norms, domestic banks must lend what share of Adjusted Net Bank Credit to priority sectors?
questions.e: Domestic scheduled commercial banks must direct 40% of Adjusted Net Bank Credit to priority sectors, including 18% to agriculture (10% to small and marginal farmers).

questions.subject: Banking
questions.q: The Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code, 2016 designates which body as the adjudicating authority for companies?
questions.e: Under the IBC, 2016, the National Company Law Tribunal is the adjudicating authority for corporate insolvency; DRTs handle individual insolvency.

questions.subject: Banking
questions.q: NARCL, often called India's 'bad bank', was set up in —
questions.e: The National Asset Reconstruction Company Ltd was incorporated in 2021 to acquire and resolve stressed assets of public sector banks.

questions.subject: Banking
questions.q: Under Basel III norms as implemented in India, banks must maintain a minimum CRAR (including capital conservation buffer) of —
questions.e: Indian banks must maintain 9% minimum CRAR plus a 2.5% capital conservation buffer, i.e. 11.5% total under Basel III.

questions.subject: Banking
questions.q: The Cash Reserve Ratio was cut by 100 basis points to 3% in — ⚠verify
questions.e: The RBI cut the CRR by 100 bps to 3% in June 2025 (in tranches) to inject durable liquidity. ⚠verify

questions.subject: Banking
questions.q: The Statutory Liquidity Ratio currently stands at —
questions.e: Banks must maintain 18% of net demand and time liabilities as SLR in approved securities.

questions.subject: Banking
questions.q: Bank credit growth at the end of the June quarter of 2026 stood at —
questions.e: RBI's August 2026 monthly bulletin noted bank credit growth of 18.3% at the end of the June quarter, indicating strong lending momentum.

questions.subject: Banking
questions.q: The International Financial Services Centres Authority (IFSCA) is headquartered at —
questions.e: IFSCA, established in 2020 as the unified regulator for IFSCs, is headquartered at GIFT City, Gandhinagar.

questions.subject: Banking
questions.q: The Pension Fund Regulatory and Development Authority was established in —
questions.e: PFRDA was set up in 2003; it regulates the National Pension System and the Atal Pension Yojana.

questions.subject: Banking
questions.q: IRDAI, the insurance regulator, is headquartered in —
questions.e: The Insurance Regulatory and Development Authority of India (established 1999) is headquartered in Hyderabad.

questions.subject: Banking
questions.q: Small Finance Banks are required to extend what share of their Adjusted Net Bank Credit to priority sectors?
questions.e: Small Finance Banks must direct 75% of their Adjusted Net Bank Credit to priority sector lending.

questions.subject: Banking
questions.q: The Account Aggregator framework in India was introduced by —
questions.e: The RBI introduced the Account Aggregator framework (NBFC-AA licence category, 2016) to enable consent-based sharing of financial data.

questions.subject: Banking
questions.q: TReDS, the platform for discounting MSME trade receivables, was conceptualised in —
questions.e: The RBI conceptualised Trade Receivables Discounting System in 2014; platforms like RXIL, M1xchange and Invoicemart operate under it.

questions.subject: Banking
questions.q: The SARFAESI Act, which empowers banks to enforce security interests without court intervention, was enacted in —
questions.e: The Securitisation and Reconstruction of Financial Assets and Enforcement of Security Interest Act was enacted in 2002.

questions.subject: Banking
questions.q: Regional Rural Banks were established in 1975 under —
questions.e: Regional Rural Banks were set up in 1975 and are governed by the Regional Rural Banks Act, 1976, with ownership shared by the Centre, sponsor banks and state governments.

questions.subject: Banking
questions.q: The Lead Bank Scheme, assigning a lead bank to each district, was introduced in —
questions.e: The Lead Bank Scheme was introduced in 1969 following the Gadgil Study Group's recommendations to coordinate banking development at the district level.

questions.subject: Banking
questions.q: Which of the following institutions is a wholly owned subsidiary of the RBI?
questions.e: The Deposit Insurance and Credit Guarantee Corporation is a wholly owned subsidiary of the RBI; NABARD and SIDBI are separate institutions.

questions.subject: Culture
questions.q: Sarnath was inscribed as India's 45th UNESCO World Heritage Site on —
questions.e: Sarnath was inscribed on 25 July 2026 during the 48th session of the World Heritage Committee in Busan, South Korea, becoming India's 45th World Heritage property.

questions.subject: Culture
questions.q: India's 45 World Heritage Sites comprise —
questions.e: India's 45 sites comprise 37 cultural, 7 natural and 1 mixed property (Khangchendzonga National Park), placing India 6th globally.

questions.subject: Culture
questions.q: Sarnath is revered in Buddhism because —
o: the Buddha delivered his first sermon there
questions.e: Sarnath (Varanasi, UP) is where the Buddha delivered his first sermon — the Dhammacakkappavattana — to his five disciples; it has been on India's tentative list since 1998.

questions.subject: Culture
questions.q: The UNESCO inscription of Sarnath includes which of the following components?
o: Chaukhandi Stupa and the archaeological remains
questions.e: The serial inscription 'Sarnath' covers the ancient site with its stupas, monasteries and temples, and the Chaukhandi Stupa — marking the spot where the Buddha met his first disciples.

questions.subject: Culture
questions.q: With 45 sites, India ranks which in the world for the number of UNESCO World Heritage properties?
questions.e: India ranks 6th globally with 45 sites, behind Italy, China, France, Germany and Spain.

questions.subject: Culture
questions.q: The 'Maratha Military Landscapes of India', inscribed in 2025, consists of —
o: 10 sea forts of the Konkan coast
12 forts across Maharashtra and Tamil Nadu
questions.e: Inscribed at the 47th session in Paris (2025) as India's 44th site, the Maratha Military Landscapes comprise 12 forts — 11 in Maharashtra and Gingee Fort in Tamil Nadu.

questions.subject: Culture
questions.q: Who was announced as the recipient of the Dadasaheb Phalke Award in September 2025?
questions.e: Malayalam superstar Mohanlal was announced for the Dadasaheb Phalke Award in September 2025; he is the second Malayali recipient after Adoor Gopalakrishnan (2004).

questions.subject: Culture
questions.q: The 59th Jnanpith Award (for 2024) was conferred on —
questions.e: Hindi writer Vinod Kumar Shukla received the 59th Jnanpith Award (for 2024), announced in March 2025.

questions.subject: Culture
questions.q: As of 2026, the state with the highest number of GI tags in India is —
questions.e: Uttar Pradesh leads India's GI tally with more than 75 registered products, out of roughly 658 GI tags nationwide.

questions.subject: Culture
questions.q: Under the Geographical Indications of Goods Act, 1999, a GI registration is valid for —
questions.e: GI registration under the 1999 Act is valid for 10 years and renewable; India's first GI tag was Darjeeling Tea (2004-05).

questions.subject: Culture
questions.q: Which of the following received a GI tag from Uttar Pradesh in 2026?
questions.e: Banaras Thandai (along with Banaras Tabla and Banaras Shehnai) was among the new 2026 GI registrations from Uttar Pradesh.

questions.subject: Culture
questions.q: The Bodo 'Dokhona' and Garo textile weaving, newly GI-tagged, belong to —
questions.e: The Bodo Dokhona (Assam) and Garo Dakmanda textile weaving (Meghalaya) received GI tags, recognising the Northeast's handloom heritage.

questions.subject: Culture
questions.q: 'Woraiyur cotton sari', GI-tagged in January 2026, is woven in —
questions.e: The Woraiyur cotton sari of Tiruchi was among five Tamil Nadu products GI-tagged in January 2026, alongside Kavindapadi nattu sakkarai and Namakkal's soapstone cookware.

questions.subject: Culture
questions.q: 'Ponduru Khadi', which received a GI tag, comes from —
questions.e: Ponduru Khadi of Srikakulam district, Andhra Pradesh — hand-spun and hand-woven — received its GI tag recognising a century-old tradition.

questions.subject: Culture
questions.q: Which Bihar product was among the 28 GI registrations facilitated by NABARD in July 2026?
questions.e: NABARD facilitated 28 new GI registrations (July 2026), including Bihar's Nalanda Bawanbuti saree and fabrics and Gaya's Pattharkatti stone craft.

questions.subject: Culture
questions.q: 'Kuchai Silk', newly GI-tagged, is a product of —
questions.e: Kuchai Silk of Jharkhand's Seraikela-Kharsawan region — tribal women rear the silk on sal trees — was among the 2026 GI additions.

questions.subject: Culture
questions.q: The Bihu 'Pepa', which received a GI tag, is —
o: a buffalo-horn musical instrument of Assam
a rice beer of Arunachal Pradesh
questions.e: The Pepa, the buffalo-horn wind instrument synonymous with Assam's Bihu dance, received a GI tag along with other Assam bamboo crafts.

questions.subject: Culture
questions.q: Which Ladakh product received a GI tag?
questions.e: Ladakh Seabuckthorn received a GI tag, joining Raktsey Karpo Apricot and other Ladakhi products in the GI registry.

questions.subject: Culture
questions.q: How many languages currently enjoy classical language status in India?
questions.e: With the October 2024 addition of Marathi, Pali, Prakrit, Assamese and Bengali, India has 11 classical languages.

questions.subject: Culture
questions.q: The 182-metre Statue of Unity at Ekta Nagar, Gujarat, depicts —
questions.e: The Statue of Unity (182 m, the world's tallest statue) depicts Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel and stands at Ekta Nagar (Kevadia), Gujarat.

questions.subject: Culture
questions.q: Which site on India's UNESCO tentative list is known for its megalithic menhirs?
questions.e: Mudumal in Telangana, with its megalithic menhirs, is on India's tentative list alongside the Kanger Valley, Chausath Yogini temples and Gupta temples.

questions.subject: Culture
questions.q: The Kanger Valley National Park, on India's UNESCO tentative list, is in —
questions.e: Kanger Valley National Park in Chhattisgarh's Bastar region — home to the state bird, the Bastar Hill Myna — is on India's tentative list.

questions.subject: Culture
questions.q: The Chaukhandi Stupa at Sarnath marks the spot where —
o: the Buddha met his first disciples
the Buddha delivered the Fire Sermon
questions.e: The Chaukhandi Stupa marks the spot where the Buddha met his first disciples; it is part of the Sarnath serial inscription on the World Heritage List.

questions.subject: Culture
questions.q: 'Chausath Yogini' temples, on India's tentative list, are dedicated to —

questions.subject: Culture
questions.q: Which of the following is NOT a classical language of India?
questions.e: Maithili is a scheduled (Eighth Schedule) language but not a classical language; Pali, Prakrit and Odia all hold classical status.

questions.subject: Culture

questions.e: Namakkal's makkal pathirangal (soapstone vessels) was GI-tagged in January 2026 with the Woraiyur cotton sari and Thooyamalli rice.

questions.subject: Culture
questions.q: Gaya's 'Pattharkatti' stone craft, GI-registered in 2026, is from —
questions.e: Gaya Pattharkatti stone craft of Bihar was among the 28 GI registrations facilitated by NABARD in July 2026.

questions.subject: Culture
questions.q: India's mixed World Heritage Site (cultural + natural) is —
questions.e: Khangchendzonga National Park (Sikkim) is India's only mixed World Heritage Site; the other 44 are 37 cultural and 7 natural.

questions.subject: Culture
questions.q: The 'Ambasamudram choppu saman', GI-tagged in January 2026, refers to —
questions.e: Ambasamudram choppu saman — traditional wooden toys of Tamil Nadu — was GI-tagged in January 2026 alongside the Woraiyur cotton sari.

questions.subject: Culture
questions.q: The Buddha's first sermon at Sarnath is known as —
questions.e: The Buddha's first sermon at Sarnath — setting in motion the wheel of dhamma — is recorded as the Dhammacakkappavattana Sutta.

questions.subject: Economy
questions.q: India's real GDP grew by what percentage in Q1 of FY2026-27 (April–June 2026)?
questions.e: India's real GDP grew 7.8% in Q1 FY2026-27 (April–June 2026), with real GVA up 8.2% and nominal GDP up 10.3%.

questions.subject: Economy
questions.q: The RBI's real GDP growth forecast for FY2026-27 is —
questions.e: The RBI retained its FY2026-27 real GDP growth forecast at 6.7% in August 2026; S&P projected 7% and Fitch 6.9%.

questions.subject: Economy
questions.q: The Union Budget 2026-27 raised capital expenditure to —
questions.e: Budget 2026-27 allocated ₹12.2 lakh crore for capex (4.4% of GDP), continuing the infrastructure push.

questions.subject: Economy
questions.q: The fiscal deficit target for FY2026-27 is —
questions.e: Budget 2026-27 targets a fiscal deficit of 4.3% of GDP, with central government debt-to-GDP projected at 55.6%.

questions.subject: Economy
questions.q: Total expenditure budgeted for FY2026-27 is —
questions.e: Budget 2026-27 pegs total expenditure at ₹53.5 lakh crore, with net tax receipts of ₹28.7 lakh crore.

questions.subject: Economy
questions.q: The new Income Tax Act, 2025 came into force on —
questions.e: The new Income Tax Act, 2025 took effect on 1 April 2026, replacing the 1961 Act; the ITR filing date for non-audit cases moved to 31 August.

questions.subject: Economy
questions.q: In Budget 2026-27, Securities Transaction Tax on futures and options was —
o: raised, to 0.05% on futures and 0.15% on options
questions.e: Budget 2026-27 raised STT to 0.05% on futures and 0.15% on options to curb speculative derivatives trading.

questions.subject: Economy
questions.q: Budget 2026-27 changed the taxation of share buybacks to treat them as —
questions.e: Buybacks are now taxed as capital gains in shareholders' hands, closing the earlier route of tax treatment as exempt income.

questions.subject: Economy
questions.q: Budget 2026-27 reduced Tax Collected at Source on overseas tour packages, education and medical remittances to —
questions.e: TCS on overseas tour packages, education and medical purposes was cut to 2%, easing compliance for travellers and students.

questions.subject: Economy
questions.q: Budget 2026-27 made Minimum Alternate Tax of 14% —
o: the final tax, with no carry-forward of MAT credit
questions.e: Budget 2026-27 made 14% MAT the final tax, ending the carry-forward of MAT credit disputes.

questions.subject: Economy
questions.q: Budget 2026-27 offered foreign cloud and data-centre companies a tax holiday until —
questions.e: Foreign companies providing cloud services through Indian data centres get a tax holiday until 2047, aligning with the Viksit Bharat horizon.

questions.subject: Economy
questions.q: The nominal GDP growth assumption in Budget 2026-27 is —
questions.e: Budget 2026-27 assumes 10% nominal GDP growth for the year.

questions.subject: Economy
questions.q: India became the world's fourth-largest economy in 2025, surpassing —
questions.e: India overtook Japan in 2025 to become the world's fourth-largest economy (IMF data), as noted by NITI Aayog's CEO in May 2025.

questions.subject: Economy
questions.q: India–EU free trade agreement negotiations were concluded on —
questions.e: India and the EU concluded FTA negotiations on 27 January 2026, ending talks that began in 2007 and were relaunched in 2022; EU signature and ratification steps remained pending in September 2026.

questions.subject: Economy
questions.q: The 'GST 2.0' rationalisation of September 2025 simplified the slab structure to —
questions.e: The GST Council's September 2025 reform moved to two main slabs of 5% and 18% (plus 40% on sin and luxury goods), effective 22 September 2025.

questions.subject: Economy
questions.q: In August 2025, total US tariffs on Indian goods reached 50% because —
o: India raised tariffs on US goods first
an additional 25% was imposed over Russian oil purchases, on top of 25% reciprocal tariffs
questions.e: The US imposed 25% reciprocal tariffs and then an additional 25% penalty over India's Russian oil purchases (effective 27 August 2025), taking total tariffs to 50%.

questions.subject: Economy
questions.q: The India–UK Comprehensive Economic and Trade Agreement was signed in —
questions.e: The India–UK CETA was signed in London in July 2025, India's first major FTA with a developed Western economy in years.

questions.subject: Economy
questions.q: Google announced a $15 billion AI data centre investment in —
questions.e: Google announced a $15 billion AI data centre in Visakhapatnam (October 2025), among the largest such investments in India.

questions.subject: Economy
questions.q: Budget 2026-27 announced how many new high-speed rail corridors?
questions.e: Budget 2026-27 announced seven new high-speed rail corridors, the Dankuni–Surat dedicated freight corridor and 20 new national waterways.

questions.subject: Economy
questions.q: Budget 2026-27 proposed developing 'City Economic Regions' centred on —
questions.e: Budget 2026-27 proposed City Economic Regions around Tier-II and Tier-III cities as new growth engines.

questions.subject: Economy
questions.q: A high-level committee announced in Budget 2026-27 will work to raise the services sector's contribution to —
questions.e: Budget 2026-27 set up a high-level committee to increase the services sector's contribution to 10% by 2047.

questions.subject: Economy
questions.q: Which of the following was proposed in Budget 2026-27 to help industry in smaller cities?
o: a ban on new factories in metros
'Corporate Mitras' in Tier-II and Tier-III towns
questions.e: Budget 2026-27 proposed 'Corporate Mitras' — facilitation centres for businesses — in Tier-II and Tier-III towns.

questions.subject: Economy
questions.q: Budget 2026-27 proposed an integrated Customs system to be operational within —
questions.e: Budget 2026-27 proposed a fully integrated Customs system within two years to speed up clearances.

questions.subject: Economy
questions.q: Budget 2026-27 exempted how many cancer drugs from basic customs duty?
questions.e: Seventeen cancer drugs were exempted from basic customs duty in Budget 2026-27, continuing the 2025-26 exemption of 36 life-saving drugs.

questions.subject: Economy
questions.q: Advance rulings under the new tax regime will remain valid for —
questions.e: Budget 2026-27 extended the validity of advance rulings to five years to give investors tax certainty.

questions.subject: Places
questions.q: The 2026 Chess Olympiad (open and women's sections) was held in —
questions.e: The 2026 Chess Olympiad was hosted in Samarkand, Uzbekistan (16–27 September 2026), where the hosts won the open gold.

questions.subject: Places
questions.q: COP31 (November 2026) is being hosted in —
questions.e: COP31 meets in Antalya, Türkiye, from 9–20 November 2026, with Türkiye holding the presidency and Australia leading the formal negotiations.

questions.subject: Places
questions.q: The 48th session of the UNESCO World Heritage Committee (July 2026) was held in —
questions.e: The 48th WHC session in Busan inscribed Sarnath as India's 45th World Heritage Site on 25 July 2026.

questions.subject: Places
questions.q: The 72nd National Film Awards ceremony (September 2026) was held at —
questions.e: The 72nd NFA ceremony was held on 22 September 2026 at Ekta Nagar (Kevadia), Gujarat — the first time the ceremony moved outside Delhi.

questions.subject: Places
questions.q: The 20th Asian Games (2026) are being hosted by —
questions.e: The 20th Asian Games run from 19 September to 4 October 2026 in Aichi-Nagoya, Japan.

questions.subject: Places
questions.q: The FIFA World Cup 2026 final was played at —
questions.e: Spain beat Argentina 1–0 after extra time in the final at MetLife Stadium, East Rutherford, New Jersey, on 19 July 2026.

questions.subject: Places
questions.q: The 2026 ICC Men's T20 World Cup final was played at —
questions.e: India beat New Zealand by 96 runs in the final at Ahmedabad's Narendra Modi Stadium on 8 March 2026.

questions.subject: Places
questions.q: Both the Asia Cup 2025 final and the Women's Asia Cup 2026 final were played in —
questions.e: India beat Pakistan in the Asia Cup 2025 final and Sri Lanka in the Women's Asia Cup 2026 final, both in Dubai.

questions.subject: Places
questions.q: Google's $15 billion AI data centre (announced October 2025) is coming up in —
questions.e: Google announced a $15 billion AI data centre investment in Visakhapatnam, Andhra Pradesh.

questions.subject: Places
questions.q: The Pre-COP meeting ahead of COP31 (5–8 October 2026) is hosted by —
questions.e: Fiji hosts the Pre-COP from 5–8 October 2026 ahead of the Antalya summit.

questions.subject: Places
questions.q: The Ramon Magsaysay Awards ceremony for 2026 is scheduled in —
questions.e: The 2026 Ramon Magsaysay Awards will be presented in Manila on 15 November 2026.

questions.subject: Places
questions.q: India's human spaceflight missions launch from —
questions.e: ISRO's launches, including the Gaganyaan uncrewed mission targeted for 2026, lift off from the Satish Dhawan Space Centre, Sriharikota.

questions.subject: Places
questions.q: Ladakh's GI-tagged Seabuckthorn grows mainly in the valley of —
questions.e: Ladakh Seabuckthorn — GI-tagged in 2026 — grows wild across Nubra, Changthang and Indus valley belts of Ladakh.

questions.subject: Places
questions.q: The Kanger Valley National Park is located in —
questions.e: Kanger Valley National Park in Bastar, Chhattisgarh, is on India's UNESCO tentative list.

questions.subject: Places
questions.q: Sarnath, India's 45th World Heritage Site, is located near —
questions.e: Sarnath lies near Varanasi, Uttar Pradesh, where the Buddha gave his first sermon.

questions.subject: Places
questions.q: Gingee Fort, part of the Maratha Military Landscapes World Heritage Site, is in —
questions.e: Gingee Fort in Tamil Nadu is the only fort of the 12-fort Maratha Military Landscapes serial site located outside Maharashtra.

questions.subject: Places
questions.q: GIFT City, home to the IFSCA headquarters, is in —
questions.e: The International Financial Services Centres Authority is headquartered at GIFT City, Gandhinagar.

questions.subject: Places
questions.q: Ponduru, famous for its GI-tagged khadi, is in —
questions.e: Ponduru Khadi of Srikakulam district, Andhra Pradesh, received its GI tag for the century-old hand-spun tradition.

questions.subject: Places
questions.q: Mudumal, known for megalithic menhirs on India's tentative list, is in —
questions.e: Mudumal in Telangana's Narayanpet district, with its ancient menhirs, is on India's UNESCO tentative list.

questions.subject: Places
questions.q: The 2026 Chess Olympiad host city Samarkand is famous in history as —
o: a port on the Caspian Sea
a Silk Road city of Uzbekistan
questions.e: Samarkand, the historic Silk Road city of Uzbekistan, hosted the 2026 Chess Olympiad.

questions.subject: Awards
questions.q: The 2026 Ramon Magsaysay Awards were announced on 31 August 2026 for —
o: Tommy Koh, Runa Khan and Bo Kyi
questions.e: The 2026 Ramon Magsaysay laureates are Tommy Koh (Singapore), Runa Khan (Bangladesh) and Bo Kyi (Myanmar), announced on 31 August 2026.

questions.subject: Awards
questions.q: Tommy Koh, 2026 Ramon Magsaysay laureate, is best known for —
o: leading the Red Cross in Asia
presiding over the UN Conference on the Law of the Sea
questions.e: Tommy Koh of Singapore presided over the Third UN Conference on the Law of the Sea that produced UNCLOS, and is a veteran diplomat-scholar.

questions.subject: Awards
questions.q: Runa Khan, 2026 Ramon Magsaysay laureate, founded which organisation?
questions.e: Runa Khan founded Friendship (Bangladesh), which runs hospital ships and services for char (river-island) communities.

questions.subject: Awards
questions.q: Bo Kyi, 2026 Ramon Magsaysay laureate, co-founded —
o: the Assistance Association for Political Prisoners (Myanmar)
questions.e: Bo Kyi co-founded the Assistance Association for Political Prisoners in 2000 after spending seven years as a political prisoner in Myanmar.

questions.subject: Awards
questions.q: Before the 2026 announcement, how many awardees had received the Ramon Magsaysay Award in total?
questions.e: Before 2026, 356 individuals and organisations had received the Ramon Magsaysay Award; the three 2026 laureates take the total to 359.

questions.subject: Awards
questions.q: Which film won Best Feature Film at the 72nd National Film Awards?
questions.e: Article 370 (Hindi) won Best Feature Film at the 72nd National Film Awards, announced 18 July 2026.

questions.subject: Awards
questions.q: At the 72nd National Film Awards, the Best Actor honour was shared by —
o: Shah Rukh Khan and Vikrant Massey
questions.e: Kartik Aaryan (Chandu Champion) and Mammootty (Bramayugam) shared the Best Actor award at the 72nd NFAs.

questions.subject: Awards
questions.q: Who won Best Actress at the 72nd National Film Awards?
questions.e: Yami Gautam won Best Actress for Article 370 at the 72nd National Film Awards.

questions.subject: Awards
questions.q: The Best Director award at the 72nd National Film Awards went to —
o: Randeep Hooda for Swatantrya Veer Savarkar
questions.e: Rajkumar Periasamy won Best Director for Amaran (Tamil) at the 72nd National Film Awards.

questions.subject: Awards
questions.q: The 72nd National Film Awards ceremony was historic because —
o: it was held outside Delhi for the first time, at Ekta Nagar
it had no Best Actor award
questions.e: The 22 September 2026 ceremony at Ekta Nagar, Gujarat, was the first National Film Awards presentation held outside Delhi.

questions.subject: Awards
questions.q: Mohanlal was selected for the Dadasaheb Phalke Award, announced in —
questions.e: Mohanlal's Dadasaheb Phalke Award was announced in September 2025 and conferred by President Droupadi Murmu.

questions.subject: Awards
questions.q: The 59th Jnanpith Award (for 2024) went to Hindi writer —
questions.e: Vinod Kumar Shukla received the 59th Jnanpith Award (for 2024), announced in March 2025.

questions.subject: Awards
questions.q: Which film won the award for Best Film Providing Wholesome Entertainment at the 72nd NFAs?
questions.e: Kalki 2898 AD (Telugu) won the Best Film Providing Wholesome Entertainment award at the 72nd National Film Awards.

questions.subject: Awards
questions.q: Which film won the Best Hindi Film award at the 72nd National Film Awards?
questions.e: Srikanth (Hindi) won the Best Hindi Film award at the 72nd National Film Awards.
